title: Intento Means I Am Trying
voice_notes: Warm, patient teacher. One voice. Brian v3. English prompts use language_code en; Spanish reveals use language_code es. Avoid Language Transfer branding.

segments.say: One Spanish word lets you say I try and I am trying.
Intento can mean I try, or I am trying. Context does the rest.
segments.show:
intento =
I try / I am trying

segments.say: Now attach lo to the end of an unchanged verb.
Publish goes through publication, then publicación, then publicar.
Now say: I am trying to publish it.
segments.word: I am trying to publish it

segments.say: Same move with administration. It gives you administrar.
Say: I am trying to administer it.
segments.word: I am trying to administer it

segments.say: Say: I am trying to imitate it.
segments.word: I am trying to imitate it

segments.say: Good. You did not memorize a sentence. You stacked intento, a verb, and lo.

caption: Intento means I try or I am trying. Stack it with verb + lo: intento publicarlo, intento administrarlo, intento imitarlo.
